Hi Sandra / Acme Procurement team,

Thanks again for the quick call yesterday. Per our discussion, this thread captures the minimal sequence we need to close out the August metering invoice and complete the entitlement transfer to your AWS account so future SaaS purchases flow through AWS Marketplace (and the metering events reconcile to your invoices).

Summary / asks: 
- Invoice dispute: you flagged a $12,450 metering line on invoice #0827 that needs to be credited (attached: acme_invoice_0827.pdf).
- Entitlement handoff: we need your AWS Marketplace SaaS product buyer ID and the target AWS Account ID to move the entitlement mapping.
- Fulfillment webhook: we will provide a short-lived metering webhook token and a deployment guide (see attachment entitlement_mapping_acme.csv for current SKU <> internal product mapping).
- Contract amendment: small MSA amendment (DocuSign link below) to allow marketplace fulfillment; this contains the billing flow language and commission split.

Immediate asks from Acme: 
1) Confirm the AWS Account ID you want entitlements mapped to (example: 123456789012).
2) Confirm you accept a prorated credit and go-forward marketplace billing (we propose the credit covers the disputed run through Aug 27).
3) Provide the contact for your cloud ops person who can receive the webhook test (name + email).

Attachments: entitlement_mapping_acme.csv (SKU mapping), draft_msa_amendment.docx (redlines to MSA), acme_invoice_0827.pdf (invoice in question).

Next steps from our side after you confirm: we will (a) issue a customer credit for the disputed line, (b) perform entitlement transfer and send you a test metering event, and (c) route future charges through AWS Marketplace and share updated reconciliation reports.

If it helps, I can book a 30-minute run-through with your procurement + cloud ops — suggested slot: today 3:30pm PT.

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel

Sandra — thanks for the note and helpful questions. Quick answers inline below.

On Tue, Sep 7, 2027 at 11:02 AM Billing Ops <billing@acme-retail.com> wrote:
> Hi Monica,
> 
> Thanks — quick clarifying questions from finance before we greenlight the MSA amendment and credit: 
> 1) Can you confirm the exact metering SKU(s) that produced the $12,450 line? Our AP team needs SKUs to map to our GL code.

Yes — the disputed row is from SKU: RW-METER-GEN-LARGE (metering category: generation_tokens). I've attached a short CSV extract (entitlement_mapping_acme.csv) with the SKU -> product name -> internal charge code mapping. That line equates to 412,500 generation tokens billed at the negotiated rate.

> 2) For the entitlement transfer, will any user-level data be migrated or is this purely a billing mapping? We need to ensure no PII crosses in that operation.

This is purely billing-level entitlement mapping. We will not move user records or PII. The entitlement object on AWS Marketplace contains product entitlement metadata (SKU, quantity, buyer account); the transfer we perform updates the buyer ID on the entitlement record. No customer data is exported from our tenant.

> 3) Who signs the amendment on Redwood's side (name + title) — our legal wants to list the signee.

Signature will be by me (Ben Carter, Head of Sales, Redwood Inference) for the commercial amendment; contracting is run through legal but Ben is the signatory for amendments under $250k.

Operational note: for the webhook test we will need a temporary endpoint on your side that accepts a POST and returns 200 within 3s. If your ops team cannot expose a public endpoint quickly, we can run the test via our staging proxy and provide logs.

Proposed resolution plan: 
- Today EOD: Redwood issues $12,450 credit against invoice 0827 and attaches accounting memo.
- Wed AM: Entitlement transfer window (we'll perform the mapping during a 15-minute maintenance window; expected no downtime).
- Wed PM: Send test metering events and reconciliation CSVs.

If that sequencing works, Monica will send DocuSign for the amendment and I'll sign.

—Ben
